transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

It is very likely a temperature regulation issue rather than the element itself. On modern electronic Belling cookers, this erratic behaviour (sometimes too hot, sometimes too cold) usually points to a failing temperature sensor or the control board interpreting its signal incorrectly. On older mechanical models, it could be a worn-out thermostat dial. To guide you correctly: does your oven have a digital display with buttons, or is it controlled by turning a physical knob? Also, when it burns food, does the cavity feel significantly hotter than the setting suggests?

its got physical knobs and a little orange neon light, no display. and i cant really tell if its hotter, but some days the cakes go black at 180 and other days my lasagne is still cold in the middle. i do cook most days so its anoying!

[Heading: Failing oven thermostat]
Since you have physical knobs and no digital display, your oven uses a mechanical thermostat to regulate heat. The erratic behaviour—burning food one day and undercooking the next on the same setting—is classic for a failing mechanical thermostat that is losing its calibration or sticking. To confirm this safely, please place an independent oven thermometer inside the cavity (away from the walls). Preheat to 180°C and leave it for about 20 minutes. Watch what the thermometer reads: if it swings wildly (e.g., goes up to 220°C then drops to 140°C) or stays consistently far off 180°C, the thermostat is likely faulty and needs replacing. If it stays steady at 180°C, the issue might be with your baking technique or the oven fan circulation.
i dont have a oven thermometer sorry. is there anything else i can check without one? the neon sometimes goes off after about 10 mins and other times seems to stay on for ages if that helps

[Heading: Failing mechanical thermostat]
The fact that your neon light (which shows when the heating element is on) behaves inconsistently—sometimes cycling off after 10 minutes and other times staying on for ages—is the key clue. In a mechanical oven, this light tracks the thermostat's action: it should flicker on and off rapidly once the oven reaches temperature to maintain heat. If it stays on for ages, the oven is overheating (burning your cakes); if it cycles too quickly or erratically, it’s cutting power prematurely (leaving your lasagne cold). This confirms that the mechanical thermostat inside the cavity is failing and losing its calibration. Because replacing this part involves opening the oven casing and working with mains electricity, you will need to call a qualified engineer to fit a new one.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

ok thanks. i cant find the model number, theres a drawer at the bottom and the label might be behind it but i havent found it. its just a belling 60cm double oven about 10 yrs old. can an engineer sort it without the number?

[Heading: Failing mechanical thermostat]
Yes, an engineer can certainly sort it without the exact model number. They will identify the specific part needed once they are there and see the internal components, or you can provide them with the serial number (often found on the same label as the model) which is usually sufficient for ordering parts. Based on your description—the erratic temperature swings and the inconsistent neon light cycling—the issue is almost certainly a failing mechanical thermostat. This part regulates the heat by switching the element on and off; when it wears out, it loses its calibration, causing the oven to overheat or underheat unpredictably. Please call an engineer to replace the thermostat. In the meantime, you can try to compensate by using your own oven thermometer (if you borrow one) to manually adjust the dial, but this is not a reliable long-term fix.
